target: route r17-oracle-barrier: "One model containing every mechanism of the paper, and a family every algorithm of the model loses on" (the difference-propagation model D, the grade identity ob:m1-grade, the invariance theorem ob:invariance, the reduction lemma ob:reduction, ob:no-permanent, the family BC(e,s) with ob:bc-values / ob:bc-lmc / ob:bc-cert / ob:bc-lower / ob:edge)

findings.defect: The clause that makes M1 a member of the model is FALSE. ob:m1-grade concludes "Consequently the preorder is produced by one (D8) step with Gamma={0,1} and Theta=(D1) from the constant least state", and ob:mem(f) asserts "the preorder M1 of def:simorder is one (D8) step, by ob:m1-grade". But (D1) is defined in ob:model as Delta -> min(Delta, L Delta), i.e. it carries a running minimum, and the coinductive iteration needs the entry at (t_1,t_0) to RISE from 0 to 1. With Gamma={0,1} and the start at the constant least state, no operator of (D1)-(D7) can ever push an entry above 0: (D1)-(D4) and (D6) are non-increasing, rho_{{0,1}} of an entry <= 0 is 0, and (D7) only writes 0 into Delta. So EVERY (D8) step of this shape returns the constant-0 matrix, whose relation is all of V x V (an unsound state), never the preorder. The mathematical core of ob:m1-grade -- the operator identity F'(R) = {(x,y) : (L chi_R)(x,y) <= 0} -- is correct and I confirmed it; only the model-membership clause fails, and with it the headline claim that the identification "puts M1 ... into one model D". Repair: define (D1) as Delta -> L Delta (the running min is then obtainable from (D6), and ob:invariance's (D1) step goes through unchanged since it only uses monotonicity of the clauses plus hypothesis (i)); or let (D8) start from the greatest state. The barrier ob:bc-lower is NOT affected: it treats M1 separately, by checking that every point of every P_k satisfies every preorder cut, which I reproduced.
findings.evidence: Independent exact-rational reimplementation (mybc.py, gr.py, d8.py, sep.py in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-audit-oracle-barrier-correctness). (a) The identity F'(R)={L chi_R <= 0} verified on 400 random relations over G_8 and G*: 0 failures. (b) Iterating rho_{{0,1}} o (D1) [with the running min] from Delta == -1: on G_8 the limit relates all 64 pairs, whereas |preorder| = 36; on G* all 361 pairs vs |preorder| = 184. Iterating rho_{{0,1}} o L [no running min] from the same start returns EXACTLY the preorder (36 and 184). (c) Starting a (D8) step from the model's own start state Delta_0 = clamp(U_Z - L_Z) with the running min gives the INDUCTIVE (lfp) reading, strictly weaker than the gfp: on the 6-vertex stopping game x->(x,a), y->(y,a), a->(t_0,t_1), m->(x,y) with m in Vmax (trap empty, w* = (1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2,0,1), Z_0={t_0}, Z_1={t_1}), (x,y) lies in the preorder (27 pairs) but not in the (D8) output (17 pairs).

findings.defect: Off-by-one in the round count. The proof establishes "no member of D_0 reports after k <= K applications"; the statement says "decides ... within K+1 = floor(ln(c/4gamma)/ln(1/a)) operator applications". The invariant Delta >= Lambda(P_k) is only guaranteed for k <= K, so the proved statement is "not within K applications". The 2^{Omega(N)} asymptotic is unaffected.
findings.evidence: ob:bc-lower's proof reads "Now let A in D_0 report after k <= K applications"; the certificate chain is P_0 ... P_K with hypotheses (i),(ii) required only for k < K.

findings.defect: "blocks all six additive and six multiplicative tests ... for exactly floor(ln(c/4gamma)/ln(1/a)) rounds" -- "exactly" is wrong; the certificate is a lower bound on the silence, and the true silence is much longer at small e. K+1 is the exact length of the certificate chain, not of the stall.
findings.evidence: On BC(2,5), K+1 = 2, but I ran the actual mechanisms (one round = (D1) then (D2) then (D4)) from the model's start state, plain and preorder-seeded, for 14 rounds: no test fires, and every round asserted sound against w*. The min-times ratio closure R^T was silent for 16 rounds.

findings.defect: The repertoire has no MULTIPLICATIVE closure, so the model omits R^T of prop:ratio-closure -- a propagation mechanism of the paper that is strictly stronger than M6 (on H_m it fires at rounds 7,11,15,20,24 where M6 stalls for 2^{Omega(N)} rounds). The route's title ("One model containing every mechanism of the paper") and ob:bc-lower's "nor any combination ... of them" therefore overstate what the model contains. The gap is repairable in one line: Lambda_x(P) obeys the multiplicative triangle inequality Lambda_x(x,z) <= Lambda_x(x,y) Lambda_x(y,z) whenever z(y) > 0 on P, so a (D2') min-times step preserves the invariant.
findings.evidence: prop:ratio-closure (frontier.tex l.13704) defines R^T. I implemented it (rt.py) with the sound conventions (0 * anything = 0; INF * 0 = INF) and ran it on BC(2,5): silent for 16 rounds, R(Q,v_0) = 1 exactly throughout. Lambda_x(P_0) on BC(2,5) has 0 violations of the multiplicative triangle inequality over all N^3 triples.

findings.defect: "Let CQ, CE, CH, Q_0 be the dyadic sink chains ... every vertex of them is average and reads only the two sinks" is false of any chain of length >= 2: a chain vertex reads the NEXT chain vertex and one sink (a chain in which every vertex reads only the two sinks realises only 0, 1/2, 1). The object is still pinned by the citation to lem:dyadic-row, and nothing downstream depends on the false clause, but as written the definition is self-contradictory.
findings.evidence: I built the chains as c_j -> (t_{b_j}, c_{j+1}), c_D -> (t_{b_D}, t_0) with b the binary expansion; lengths 2,3,2,s-1 for 1/4, 3/8, 3/4, 1/2+2^{1-s} as ob:bc states, and every closed form of ob:bc-values then reproduces exactly.

findings.defect: "No member of D evaluates a strategy: R contains no operator whose output depends on the inverse of (I - A_{sigma,tau}) for a positional pair" is false as literally read: (D3) solves an LP over Q(G;L_Z,U_Z), and lem:transport-exact says that on a successor-closed set of average vertices the constraints pin x = (I-P)^{-1} r exactly. The intended statement (no operator evaluates a FIXED positional pair on the whole game) is fine, but the sentence as written is not.
findings.evidence: lem:transport-exact, frontier.tex; and BC's dyadic chains and {g,P} are successor-closed average sets, so (D3) does compute such inverses on BC itself.

findings.defect: The multiplicative half of the proof asserts, without proof and without a GAP marker, that "all three maxima are attained at vertices of the hexagons, a linear-fractional function with positive denominator being both quasi-convex and quasi-concave". Under rule 4 this is a known theorem used without proof. It is true and has a two-line proof (max over the polytope of z(x) - t z(y) is affine, hence attained at a vertex; the max of z(x)/z(y) is the least t making that max <= 0, hence equals the vertex maximum), but the route does not give it, and both the route's and my verification of Lambda_x rest on it.
findings.evidence: ob:bc-cert's proof, paragraph beginning "The multiplicative condition at v_1".

findings.defect: ob:invariance's own stated conclusion does NOT block three of the twelve tests on BC: Lambda(P_k)(v_0,Q) = 0 <= 0 (clause (i)), Lambda(P_k)(P,Q) = 0 <= 0 (pair test), and Lambda(P_k)(B^i_1,v_i) = (b-1)l < 0 (clause (ii)). Those three are blocked by SOUNDNESS of the member's state, which ob:bc-lower's proof does invoke correctly but which ob:invariance's "decides ... only if" conclusion omits. The statement of ob:invariance is therefore weaker than the use made of it, and a reader taking ob:invariance alone would conclude the certificate fails. (Note also that w* is NOT in any P_k, so Lambda(P_k) is not itself a sound difference matrix.)
findings.evidence: My first firing sweep, using Lambda(P_k) alone, reported ('add-i',v0,Q), ('add-pair',v0,'10'), ('add-ii',v1,B1_1) as firing at every k; re-running with the effective lower bound max(Lambda(P_k)(x,y), w*(x)-w*(y)) gives zero firings at every k <= K at (2,5),(3,5),(2,6) -- exactly what ob:bc-lower's proof text says.

findings.defect: Two imprecisions in the proof: (i) "the member (D1)^k, which is exactly the slack calculus" -- the model starts at Delta_0 = clamp(U_Z - L_Z) <= 1 and (D1) carries a running min, whereas thm:slack-vi-upper is about def:slack's Delta_k from Delta_0 == 1 (the conclusion survives by monotonicity, since the model's Delta_k <= def:slack's Delta_k); (ii) it invokes ob:invariance, whose hypotheses include (ii) on the ratio clauses, although only hypothesis (i) is needed for a (D1)-only run. Also ob:model leaves (D3) undefined when K(Delta) is empty, which happens for the constant least state Delta == -1 and for Delta == 0, both reachable inside a (D8) step.
findings.evidence: ob:no-permanent's proof; def:slack's Delta_0 == 1 (frontier.tex); K(Delta) with Delta == 0 forces z(t_1) - z(t_0) = 1 <= 0, so K(Delta) = empty.

findings.defect: The step "the game K_sharp of thm:matching-barrier fools every such clause" needs the extra sub-argument of thm:matching-barrier's proof about the atom (x^{(1)},y): at (v_0,P) it interprets as the diagonal pair (P,P), and the transfer requires frame(P,P) = frame(1,1) in G_8 = frame(k,k) in K_sharp. This holds (all three have types (avg,avg,t_0 | avg,avg,t_0) and equality pattern {x=y, x^0=y^0, x^1=y^1}, and the same true-atom set), but the route does not spell it out.
findings.evidence: I verified the three frames and their true-atom sets exactly; also verified frame(m,k) in K_sharp has the same (types, equality pattern) as frame(5,1) and hence as frame(v_0,P).

findings.defect: v_1 and v_2 are NOT value-distinguishing (both successors have value 1/2 exactly), so by prop:fv-stall the stall there is vacuous in isolation; the non-vacuous content is the stall at v_0, whose successors differ by gamma = 2^{-s}. Blocking v_1 and v_2 is still necessary for the phrase "decides no controlled vertex" and it is proved and reproduced. Separately, BC(e,s) is one-player (Vmin empty), so it lies in thm:one-player's polynomial class and in thm:modulator's (mu = 2 with X = Vmax, as WD does); the route states this openly in ob:relate, and no hardness is claimed.
findings.evidence: w*(A^i_1) = w*(B^i_1) = w*(v_i) = 1/2 at every size tested; w*(P) - w*(Q) = gamma exactly; v_0 is the unique value-distinguishing controlled vertex.

verdict:
One major defect, no fatal ones; the family, the certificate and the lower bound reproduce exactly.

WHAT I REBUILT AND REPRODUCED (all exact Fraction arithmetic, written from the statements, in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-audit-oracle-barrier-correctness; the route's code was not used):
- ob:bc-values: N = 12e+2s+11, stopping (empty trap by lem:trapchar), w* by enumeration of all 2^3 positional profiles with exact first-passage solves, Z_0={t_0} and Z_1={g,t_1} by prop:qualitative's two fixed points, the lift theta in closed form (theta_Q = c e_1, theta_{A^i_1} = a e_o, theta_{B^i_1} = b e_i), v_0 the unique value-distinguishing controlled vertex with gap gamma, and the two auxiliary inequalities (theta_y = c'e_1 => w* >= c'/2, attained at D_q; theta_y = c'e_2 => w* >= 1/4 + c'/4; max value on a theta-carrying vertex = 3/4). Every vertex reachable from v_0. Sizes (e,s) = (2,5),(3,5),(4,5),(2,6),(3,8): 0 mismatches.
- ob:bc-cert / ob:invariance hypotheses, checked DIRECTLY at all N^2 entries and every k <= K, not via ob:reduction: (alpha) every vertex of P_k inside Q(G;L_Z,U_Z) with the box, sink and Z pins and the Max rows; (i) every def:slack clause at Lambda(P_k) >= Lambda(P_{k+1}), including BOTH orders of the Max/Min composite; (ii) every def:ratio clause at Lambda_x(P_k) >= Lambda_x(P_{k+1}) with the 0 / +infinity conventions. Six sizes: N = 45, 47, 57, 63, 69, 81. ZERO failures of any kind.
- ob:bc-lower's displayed quantities: Lambda(P_k)(v_0,P) = Lambda(P_k)(Q,P) = cM_k - gamma, Lambda(P_k)(Q,v_0) = 0, (1-a^2)M_k, (1-b)M_k, a(1-b)M_k, (b-a^2)M_k at v_1 and symmetrically at v_2, and Lambda_x(P_k)(Q,v_0) = 1 -- exact match at every k for (2,5),(3,5),(2,6),(2,7). With the member's soundness added (as the proof does), none of the six additive and six multiplicative tests fires at v_0, v_1, v_2 at any k <= K.
- The preorder: my gfp of def:simorder reproduces the paper's data (G_8: neither 4 <= 1 nor 1 <= 4; G*: six of the seven controlled vertices decided). On BC it is sound, transitive, decides none of the twelve pairs, and every one of its cuts is satisfied by P_0 (hence by every P_k): 0 violations at (2,5),(3,5),(2,6). The symmetric-variant remark reproduces too (eta_1 = eta_2 gives v_1 <= v_2 <= v_1 and the preorder still decides nothing).
- ob:bc-lmc's frame identities: frame(Q,P) = frame(4,1) of G_8 and frame(v_0,P) = frame(5,1), as (types, equality pattern, true-atom set), at five sizes; Pi is exactly lem:fooling-partner's set both times.
- ob:edge: all-switches from all 8 starting profiles halts within one round; S_sigma is empty and val_sigma = w* whenever sigma(v_0) = P; five sizes.
- The round-count table: all fourteen rows of K+1 reproduce exactly and agree with floor(ln(c/4gamma)/ln(1/a)) (2,5,11,22,46,93 at s=5; 4,9 at s=6; 5 at s=7; 16,34,71,144 at s=8; 49 at (4,10)), and the claimed bound floor((2^{e+1}-3)(s-4)ln2/3) holds at all fourteen.
- Cross-checks with the real mechanisms: (D1)(D2)(D4) run plain and preorder-seeded on BC(2,5) and BC(3,5) -- silent 14 rounds, sound every round; R^T (def:ratio + min-times closure) silent 16 rounds.

THE MAJOR DEFECT. ob:m1-grade's operator identity is correct (verified on 400 random relations), but its closing clause -- and ob:mem(f), and with them the route's headline that the model CONTAINS M1 -- is false: because (D1) is min(Delta, L Delta), a (D8) step with Gamma = {0,1} from the constant least state can never raise an entry above 0 and so returns the constant-0 matrix (the full relation V x V, an unsound state) on every game, not the preorder; started from the model's own initial state it returns the inductive (lfp) reading, which I separated from the preorder on an explicit 6-vertex stopping game. The repair is one word in (D1) and does not touch ob:invariance, ob:bc-cert or ob:bc-lower, all of which handle M1 by the (correct, reproduced) preorder-cut argument.

Everything else I found is minor or a note: an off-by-one in ob:bc-lower's round count, "exactly" for what is a lower bound, a self-contradictory sentence in ob:bc's chain description, a false sentence about (D3) not inverting (I - A), an unproved appeal to the vertex-attainment of linear-fractional maxima, the omission of prop:ratio-closure's min-times closure from the repertoire (repairable in one line, and I checked R^T is stalled anyway), and the fact that ob:invariance's stated conclusion is weaker than the use ob:bc-lower makes of it (soundness carries three of the twelve entries). The route's three declared GAPs are honestly and accurately stated, and its own admissions (BC is one-player, all-switches converges on it in one round, M(1,0) decides it, D(BC) = 2^{Theta(e)}) all check out.
